description: `worktrees <path> --prune --dry-run` previews two cases in one project: a plain file sitting directly under .multiverse/worktrees/ fails `_is_lane_entry` (not a directory) and is reported up front as `ignored: not a lane`, never entered into lane discovery at all; a real lane directory whose sole occupant task is recorded DONE in routing.log but whose dispatch pane (`pane=w1:p1`) Herdr's `agent list` still reports live is kept by `live_guard_reason`/`live_occupant_pane_state` (worktrees.py) rather than pruned, naming the occupant and the live pane's agent_status. `lanes()` (worktrees.py) walks the worktrees directory itself rather than `git worktree list`, so the lane directory here is a plain committed directory, not a real registered git worktree — sufficient for this command's own discovery and merged/clean checks, which is exactly why a genuine `git worktree add` is unnecessary (and, per this harness's static 'files' fixtures with no post-sandbox-creation templating, would be unconstructable here anyway: its internal .git/worktrees/*/gitdir pointer needs the sandbox's own dynamic absolute path, known only after this scenario's JSON is already fixed).
